newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks drop despite gains in power sector.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks drop despite gains in power sector.

text.p: Brazilian share prices were down by midafternoon Thursday as a rally in power stocks after the auction of a controlling stake in Bahia's Coelba utility failed to spill into the broader market, brokers said.
"The Coelba sale was good, but the market is down overall today. It doesn't have any strength," a broker at local Crefisul brokerage said.
The Bovespa index of 47 leading shares was 1.38 percent lower at 12,844 points, even as the Sao Paulo bolsa's Electrical Energy Index gained 1.38 percent at 3,611 points.
Turnover was a strong 843 million reais ($778 million). Brokers said trading was mostly lackluster, with prices sagging amid speculation and day-trading by local players.
"It's domestic day-trading," one broker said. "It's not on technicals or news. There's nothing going on today."
Most stocks dipped along with benchmark blue-chip Telebras preferred, which was down 1.66 percent at 160.3 reais. Telebras shares and options regularly account for 65 percent of total daily volume.

Power shares were the exception, bucking the downward trend after a consortium led by Spain's Iberdrola SA won a 65.64 percent voting stake in Coelba with a bid of 1.73 billion reais ($1.6 billion), about 77 percent more than the asking price.

The results of the auction on the Rio de Janeiro bolsa boosted Coelba preferred by 4.88 percent to 86 reais. But its common shares, which had risen in the run-up to the sale, dropped 2.7 percent to 108 reais.

Other power shares showed sharp gains. Sao Paulo state owned Cia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) common shares were up 2.78 percent at 222 reais, while preferred shares of Companhia Energetica de Sao Paulo SA (Cesp) at 78.00.
But preferred B shares of Eletrobras, the federal power holding company, dropped 0.77 percent to 643.99 reais amid profit-taking.
Minas Gerais state's Cemig also was higher, with its common up 1.85 percent at 54.49 reais and its preferred 1.62 percent higher at 61.99 reais.
